\section*{Question 2}

A tank contains 125 gallons of heating oil at time \(t=0\). During the time interval \(0 \leq t \leq 12\) hours, heating oil is pumped into the tank at the rate
\[
H(t)=2+\frac{10}{(1+\ln (t+1))} \text { gallons per hour. }
\]
During the same time interval, heating oil is removed from the tank at the rate
\[
R(t)=12 \sin \left(\frac{t^{2}}{47}\right) \text { gallons per hour. }
\]
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] How many gallons of heating oil are pumped into the tank during the time interval \(0 \leq t \leq 12\) hours?
\item[(b)] Is the level of heating oil in the tank rising or falling at time \(t=6\) hours? Give a reason for your answer.
\item[(c)] How many gallons of heating oil are in the tank at time \(t=12\) hours?
\item[(d)] At what time \(t\), for \(0 \leq t \leq 12\), is the volume of heating oil in the tank the least? Show the analysis that leads to your conclusion.
\item[(a)] \(\int_{0}^{12} H(t) d t=70.570\) or 70.571
\item[(b)] \(H(6)-R(6)=-2.924\), so the level of heating oil is falling at \(t=6\).
\item[(c)] \(125+\int_{0}^{12}(H(t)-R(t)) d t=122.025\) or 122.026
\item[(d)] The absolute minimum occurs at a critical point or an endpoint. \(H(t)-R(t)=0\) when \(t=4.790\) and \(t=11.318\). The volume increases until \(t=4.790\), then decreases until \(t=11.318\), then increases, so the absolute minimum will be at \(t=0\) or at \(t=11.318\).
\[
125+\int_{0}^{11.318}(H(t)-R(t)) d t=120.738
\]
Since the volume is 125 at \(t=0\), the volume is least at \(t=11.318\).
\end{itemize}
